prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an elevated camera wearer looking down into an indoor room with a brick counter and water jugs on the left (~1.5–2.5 m away in frames 1–3), a low bed/platform in the upper background (~3–4 m away), a plastic stool and white bucket on the left floor (~1.5–2 m away, ~0.3 m apart), and a counter edge entering the bottom-right foreground (~0.5–0.8 m away in frames 4–5). A young child stands on the floor below and in front of the camera wearer, starting ~2.5 m away near the brick counter in frame 1 and approaching across frames 2–5 to within ~0.8–1.0 m directly below the wearer, while the wearer's left hand enters the bottom foreground at ~0.3–0.5 m (within arm's reach) in frames 2–5 and a wall/hanging cloth occludes the left foreground at ~0.3 m in frame 2. As the child moves closer and looks upward toward the camera wearer, the child passes ~0.5 m to the right of the plastic stool and reaches arm's reach of both the wearer's extended hand and the bottom-right counter by frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground hand, left wall occlusion, and standing child from the illuminated floor despite strong flashlight glare, and shows the continuous ground-plane gradient. However, the depth map is unreliable in the upper-right corners of frames 4–5 where dimly lit floor and background objects (~2.5–4 m away) drop to uniform black, and around the bright overexposed hand and cloth where local depth contours blur together.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the approaching child in front of and below the camera wearer across all five frames (moving from ~2.5 m away on the left to ~0.8–1.0 m in the bottom center), while also masking the camera wearer's foreground left hand (~0.3–0.5 m away) in frames 2, 4, and 5. In frame 1, the child is ~0.5 m from the left counter and bucket, and by frames 4–5 the child's mask merges into a single connected pink region with the camera wearer's lower-left hand and the orange cloth on the floor, indicating they overlap in 2D projection and are within arm's reach (~0.3–0.8 m) while the child's lower legs are partly out of view at the bottom edge. While this map highlights the silhouette of the child and foreground body parts against a blacked-out background, it provides far less spatial layout information than the RGB image by omitting the room's walls, stool, counter, and bed entirely. The segmentation is highly unreliable for object identity and boundaries: in frames 1–2 it mislabels the left wall, hanging cloth, plastic stool, bucket, and floor fabrics as multiple 'person' instances and a 'kite', completely misses the wearer's hand in frame 3, and in frames 4–5 fuses the child, the wearer's hand, and the orange floor cloth into one 'person' mask.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints (yellow) of the child standing below and in front of the camera wearer across all five frames, along with a magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand in the bottom-left foreground (~0.3–0.5 m away) in frame 4. In frame 1, the child (~2.5 m away on the left) is oriented in left profile facing the brick counter within arm's reach of it, then turns in frames 2–4 to face the camera wearer with symmetric facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) angled upward toward the lens and both arms raised above shoulder height as the child approaches from ~2.2 m to ~1.2 m. By frame 5, the child is ~0.8–1.0 m away in the lower-right foreground, facing and looking up at the camera wearer with both arms lowered to rest within arm's reach on the foreground counter edge while the legs below the hips are occluded/out of the bottom frame boundary. Compared to the RGB strip, where harsh spotlight glare in frames 4–5 washes out the child's torso and the wearer's fingers, the skeleton map clearly delineates the child's shoulder-to-hip alignment, head orientation, and raised-to-lowered arm transitions. However, the pose map is unreliable where it misses the camera wearer's visible hand in frames 2, 3, and 5, drops or misplaces the child's lower-leg keypoints in frames 1, 2, and 4, and provides no spatial representation of the surrounding furniture or walls.
